text:
Sean Gallagher: kicking off a thread to nail down regression gates for Runtime LTS patch releases. We need something we can actually run on every patch + something we can enforce w/ canary. Biggest open Q: do we gate on p95 or p99 (or both)?

Neha Kapoor: +1. Also: what’s our minimum canary duration for LTS? Enterprise ops folks are going to ask “how do you know it won’t page me at 2am”.

Miles Thornton: for canary, duration alone is kind of a proxy. we should define it as BOTH time + volume. e.g. >= 2 hours AND >= N requests or >= N tokens. otherwise off-peak patches “pass” with no real signal.

Rafael Mendes: from oncall POV: p99 is where we get pain. p95 can look fine while p99 explodes due to queueing jitter. but p99 is also noisy and will block releases for random reasons.

Allison Grant: what do we have today in perf-canary? the dashboards I look at have p50/p95/p99 latency + throughput + error rate. p99 tends to fluctuate w/ low sample sizes.

Sahana Iyer: CI perspective: we can enforce the lab benchmark (synthetic) pretty deterministically (p95 and throughput). p99 in CI is going to be flaky unless we run long. for canary we can do p99 (real traffic) w/ enough volume.

Connor O'Brien: release eng needs a crisp rule we can put in a checklist. “no more than X% regression” etc. we can’t be debating per patch.

Kira Volkov: suggestion: gate CI on p95 latency + throughput + correctness tests. then canary gate on p95 AND p99 + error rate + GPU OOM/restarts. that gives us stability w/o CI flakes.

Sean Gallagher: ok, what numbers are we comfortable with? Need something strict enough to prevent slow creep but flexible for small noise.

Samir Qureshi: for LTS we should be stricter than mainline. patches are supposed to be “boring”. I’d propose:
- CI perf suite (bench-lab): p95 latency regression <= +3% vs LTS baseline, throughput regression <= -2%
- Canary (prod-like): p95 <= +3%, p99 <= +5%, and no increase in 5xx/timeouts beyond +0.05% absolute

Rafael Mendes: +5% p99 sounds reasonable. for some workloads p99 moves a lot with small changes in queue depth though. we should define how we compute (rolling 15m? 1h?)

Allison Grant: +1. p99 on 15m windows is chaos. if we define it as “over the canary window, compare p99 across the same traffic mix” it’s better.

Miles Thornton: operationally, we can do: canary runs minimum 4 hours OR until 50M tokens processed (whichever is longer). that handles low-traffic regions.

Neha Kapoor: 4h minimum seems ok. Enterprise customers often have maintenance windows; we don’t want canary to require 24h.

Connor O'Brien: 4h is workable for release day. 50M tokens might be too high for some private clusters though.

Miles Thornton: yeah that’s for our hosted/dedicated canary. for Private we can’t enforce token volume. we can provide guidance + require “smoke + perf sanity check” in the installer docs.

Sahana Iyer: for CI we should include determinism check too (repro build + stable perf). not a perf gate per se, but LTS should require it.

Sean Gallagher: let’s split requirements:
1) Required pre-merge / pre-tag checks (CI)
2) Required release-candidate canary checks (hosted/dedicated)
3) Recommended checks for Private customer canaries

Kira Volkov: also we need an escape hatch for security patches. if there’s a CVE fix and perf gate fails by 1%, we don’t want to block for a week. we need an explicit override path.

Neha Kapoor: override should page/require signoff from SRE + Runtime + Release Eng, and require explicit risk statement in notes.

Rafael Mendes: and override requires rollback plan written down (what’s the rollback trigger and who is on point).

Allison Grant: can we define rollback triggers now too? like: if error rate > +0.1% absolute or p99 > +10% sustained for 30m, auto rollback.

Miles Thornton: auto rollback is hard in private, but for hosted/dedicated we can do “rollback recommended” + a runbook step. On our side we *can* automate rollback for the canary fleet.

perf-canary-bot: FYI current perf suite metrics available for runtime candidates: p50/p95/p99 TTFT, p50/p95/p99 per-token latency, tokens/sec (throughput), GPU memory peak, kernel launch time. Baseline comparison supports thresholds per metric.

Sahana Iyer: perf-canary-bot confirms we can gate on per-token latency p95 and TTFT p95 separately (they move differently). I’d rather gate on per-token p95 and TTFT p95 (<= +3%) and throughput (<= -2%).

Samir Qureshi: +1. some patches only impact TTFT.

Sean Gallagher: ok, tentatively:
CI perf gates (bench-lab):
- TTFT p95 regression <= +3%
- Per-token latency p95 regression <= +3%
- Throughput regression <= -2%
- No new correctness failures (golden prompts + unit/integration)
- No increase in GPU OOM / crash loops in stress test

Canary gates (hosted/dedicated):
- Duration: >= 4h (or until stable volume threshold; SRE to pick a number)
- p95 end-to-end latency regression <= +3%
- p99 end-to-end latency regression <= +5%
- Error rate (5xx + upstream timeouts) increase <= +0.05% absolute
- No new sustained scheduler saturation / queue depth anomaly

Rollback triggers:
- p99 > +10% sustained 30m OR error rate > +0.1% absolute sustained 15m => rollback canary, block promotion

Does anyone object to p95 being the “primary” and p99 being “secondary but required”?

Rafael Mendes: no objection. just please specify how we compute. I suggest rolling 1h windows over the canary period + require sample size >= X requests.

Allison Grant: +1. Also call out we’ll compare vs the previous LTS patch (not mainline). Otherwise baseline jumps.

Neha Kapoor: also include “known noisy metrics are informational only” so ppl don’t argue about p99 TTFT in CI.

Connor O'Brien: can we document the “who decides” when gates are borderline? release needs a single go/no-go owner.

Sean Gallagher: go/no-go: SRE owner (me) for gates, with Runtime ack (Noah/Sofia/Hiro depending) and Release Eng ack (Connor). If disagreement -> Mateo escalation.

Miles Thornton: for canary volume threshold: propose >= 5M tokens OR >= 25k requests, whichever first, but still min 4h. That’s usually achievable.

Sahana Iyer: ok. I’ll make sure CI jobs output the baseline compare artifact so we can attach it to audit evidence later.

Kira Volkov: can we add a clause: if p99 is red but p95 is green, we must investigate + either extend canary 2h or rollback. no “ship and hope”.

Sean Gallagher: yes. rule: any p99 breach requires (a) extend canary by 2h with targeted traffic mix check OR (b) rollback. cannot promote while p99 red.

Neha Kapoor: :thumbsup: can we also mention canary should include at least 1 region w/ historically worse tail (us-east) so we don’t only canary in “happy” regions.

Miles Thornton: good call. canary fleet should be multi-region (at least 2). I’ll update rollout plan doc.

Connor O'Brien: sounds like consensus. Sean can you paste a final bullets version I can drop into the release checklist and Confluence doc?

Sean Gallagher: yep. I’ll write it up as “LTS regression gates v1” and link in the LTS docs. thanks all.

Allison Grant: last note: we should explicitly say p99 is measured end-to-end (includes queue + runtime) not just model compute. we’ve been burned by scheduler changes.

Sean Gallagher: agreed. will specify E2E latency at the API boundary for canary + compute-only in CI suite.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: also please include the escalation channel (#eng-oncall) if canary triggers rollback.

Sean Gallagher: will do.
